en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.20.
Atītārammaṇattika (The Triplet on Past Objects)
Section on Analysis:
Root Condition.
Dependent on a state with a past object, a state with a past object arises by way of root condition—[namely] a state with a past object...

Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates arise … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a past object, three aggregates arise … dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.

Dependent on a state with a future object, a state with a future object arises by way of root condition: dependent on one aggregate with a future object, three aggregates arise … [dependent on] two aggregates [two aggregates arise].
Dependent on a state with a present object, a state with a present object arises by way of root condition:

dependent on one aggregate with a present object, three aggregates arise ... [and so on] ... two aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a present object, three aggregates arise ... [and so on] ... two aggregates.
Object, etc.:
Dependent on a state with a past object, there arises a state with a past object by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*) … by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*) [note:

there is no rebirth-linking in the case of predominance] … by way of proximity-condition (*anantarapaccaya*) … by way of contiguity-condition (*samanantarapaccaya*) … by way of conascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*).

… by way of mutual condition … by way of dependence condition … by way of decisive support condition … by way of prenascence condition … by way of repetition condition (*in both prenascence and repetition, there is no rebirth-linking*) … by way of kamma condition … by way of resultant condition (*the resultant has one aggregate with a past object;
three questions are also complete. Rebirth-linking during the course of existence should be performed*).

… by way of nutriment-condition … by way of faculty-condition … by way of jhāna-condition … by way of path-condition … by way of association-condition … by way of dissociation-condition … by way of presence-condition … by way of absence-condition … by way of disappearance-condition … by way of non-disappearance-condition.
Section on Enumeration.

In the pure root condition there are three; in the object condition, three; in the predominance condition, three … (three in all cases) … in the disappearance condition, three; in the non-disappearance condition, three. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive.
1.20.1.2. Analysis of the Negative Section on Conditions (Paccayapaccanīya Vibhaṅgavāra):
Not-root (Nahetu)
Dependent on a state with a past object, a state with a past object arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate with a past object,

three aggregates arise … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … dependent on doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion arises.
Dependent on a state with a future object, a state with a future object arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate with a future object, three aggregates [arise] ... two aggregates ...
dependent on doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion [arises].
Dependent on a state with a present object, a state with a present object arises by way of the not-root condition:
dependent on one rootless aggregate with a present object,

three aggregates arise … two aggregates … at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking … dependent on doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied aggregates, doubt-accompanied or restlessness-accompanied delusion arises.
Dependent on a state with a past object, through the condition of not-predominance, there arises a state with a past object. (This is similar to the positive concomitance of co-nascence.
Not-prenascence.

Dependent on a state with a past object, a state with a past object arises by way of not-prenascence condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with a past object … two aggregates … [and so on] … at the moment of rebirth-linking … [and so on].

Dependent on a state with a future object, a state with a future object arises by way of not-prenascence condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with a future object, three aggregates arise … two aggregates … [and so on].

Dependent on a state with a present object, a state with a present object arises by way of not-prenascence condition: at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one aggregate with a present object … [and so on] … dependent on two aggregates … [and so on] … [Regarding] not-postnascence, etc.:
Dependent on a state with a past object, a state with a past object arises by way of not-postnascence condition …
Condition by way of non-repetition (*na-āsevanapaccayā*) [is similar to non-predominance] ... Condition by way of non-kamma (*nakammapaccayā*):

volition with a past object arises in dependence on aggregates with a past object. A state with a future object arises in dependence on a state with a future object by way of non-kamma condition: volition with a future object arises in dependence on aggregates with a future object.

Dependent on a state with a present object, there arises a state with a present object by way of non-kamma condition: dependent on aggregates with a present object, volition with a present object arises.
[Non-resultant:
Dependent on a state with a past object, there arises a state with a past object by way of non-resultant condition ... [etc. (In the case of non-resultant, there is no rebirth-linking.)

Dependent on a state with a present object through the condition of non-jhāna, a state with a present object arises: dependent on one aggregate accompanied by the fivefold sense-consciousness, three aggregates arise … pe … dependent on two aggregates … pe ….
(Not-path)

Dependent on a state with a past object, a state with a past object arises by way of not-path condition: dependent on one rootless aggregate with a past object, three aggregates arise ... [and so on] ... (Three questions are the same as for the not-root condition; delusion is absent. Non-dissociation:

Dependent on a state with a past object, a state with a past object arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with a past object, three aggregates arise ... [and so on] ... dependent on two aggregates ... [and so on] ...

Dependent on a state with a future object, a state with a future object arises by way of non-dissociation condition: in the immaterial plane, dependent on one aggregate with a future object, three aggregates arise …pe… dependent on two aggregates …pe….
Section on Enumeration:
Pure.

With not-root: three; with not-predominance, not-prenascence, not-postnascence, not-repetition, not-kamma, and not-resultant: three; with not-jhāna: one; with not-path: three; with not-dissociation: two. (Thus it should be counted. The Negative. 1.20.1.3.
Positive-Negative Conditionality.
Hetuduka:

With root condition, there are three [answers] for non-predominance; three for non-prenascence, non-postnascence, non-repetition, non-kamma, and non-resultant; and two for non-dissociation. (Thus it should be counted.
Positive-Negative.
1.20.1.4. Positive-Negative Conditionality (Paccayapaccanīyānuloma):

With the non-root condition (nahetupaccaya), there are three [results] in the object condition (ārammaṇa) …pe… (three in all cases) … three in the non-disappearance condition (avigata). (It should be counted in this manner.
This concludes the Positive-Negative Conditionality.
The Section on Dependence (Paṭiccavāra). 1.20.2–6.
The Chapter on Conascent Condition, Support, Conjoined, and Associated (The chapters on conascence, condition, support, conjunction, and association are similar to the chapter on dependence).
1.20.7. Chapter on Questions (Pañhāvāra) 1.20.7.1.
Positive Order of Conditions (Paccayānuloma):
Section on Analysis (Vibhaṅgavāra)
A state with a past object is related to a state with a past object by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Roots with a past object are related to their associated aggregates by way of the root condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, [roots] with a past object...
Roots are related to their associated aggregates by way of root-condition.
A state with a future object is related to a state with a future object by way of root-condition: roots having a future object are related to their associated aggregates by way of root-condition.
A state with a present object is related to a state with a present object by way of root-condition: [roots] having a present object...

Roots are a condition by way of root-condition for their associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking, roots having a present object are a condition by way of root-condition for their associated aggregates.
Object...
A state with a past object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a past object: one reviews a past sphere of infinite consciousness;
one reviews the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. One reviews past knowledge of the modes of supernormal power with a past object;
one reviews knowledge of penetration into others' minds … knowledge of recollection of past lives … knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds with a past object.
The Noble Ones review defilements that have been abandoned with respect to past objects; they review defilements that have been suppressed;
they know defilements formerly practiced. They practice insight into past aggregates with respect to past objects as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
they relish them and take delight in them. Taking that as an object, lust with respect to past objects arises, as does wrong view.
... pe ... doubt ... pe ... restlessness ... pe ... grief arises.

Past aggregates with past objects are related to knowledge of the minds of others (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*), knowledge of recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa*), knowledge of the passing away and rebirth according to karma (*yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa*), and advertence (*āvajjanā*) by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
A state with past objects is related to a state with future objects by way of object-condition—the future [state].
He reviews the base of infinite consciousness; he reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

He reviews future supernormal knowledge (iddhividha-ñāṇa) that has a past object; he reviews knowledge of the minds of others (cetopariya-ñāṇa) … [and so on] … he reviews knowledge of recollecting past lives (pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa) … [and so on] … he reviews knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their deeds (yathākammūpaga-ñāṇa). [He contemplates] the future aggregates that have a past object as impermanent … [and so on].
One contemplates, relishes, and delights in them; with that as an object, lust with a future object arises … pe … grief arises.
Future aggregates with past objects are related to knowledge of penetration of others' minds, knowledge of future existences, and adverting by way of object condition.
A state with a past object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a present object:

by means of knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a present mind that has a past object. Present aggregates with a past object are a condition, by way of object-condition, for knowledge of penetration into others' minds and for adverting.
A state with a future object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a future object:

one reviews future supernormal knowledge (iddhividha-ñāṇa) having a future object; [one reviews] knowledge of others' minds (cetopariya-ñāṇa) … knowledge of the future (anāgataṃsa-ñāṇa) … one contemplates with insight the future aggregates having a future object as impermanent … [and so forth] … one relishes them and delights in them; that [delight] … [is a condition].
Taking [the future] as object, lust arises with the future as its object … pe … grief arises.
Future aggregates with the future as their object are related to knowledge of others' minds, knowledge of future states, and adverting by way of object condition.
A state with the future as its object is related to a state with the past as its object by way of object condition—[namely,] the future as object … [and so on].
He reviews past knowledge of supernormal powers, knowledge of the minds of others, and knowledge of future states...
[and so on] ...Noble ones review defilements abandoned with respect to the future object; they review defilements suppressed.
They know defilements formerly practiced. With respect to the future object, they practice insight into the past aggregates as impermanent... [and so on] ...into suffering, and into non-self.
One relishes and delights in it; with that as its object, lust with a past object arises …pe… grief arises.

Past aggregates with a future object are related to knowledge of penetration into others' minds, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of the destiny of beings according to their deeds, and to adverting, by way of object-condition.
A state with a future object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a present object:
through the knowledge of penetration of others' minds (cetopariyañāṇa), one knows the mind of one possessing a present mind that has a future object.
Present aggregates with a future object are a condition, by way of object-condition, for the knowledge of penetration of others' minds and for adverting.
A state with a present object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a present object:
through the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, one knows the mind of one possessing a present mind that has a present object.
Present aggregates with a present object are a condition, by way of object-condition, for the knowledge of penetration into others' minds and for adverting.
A state with a present object is related to a state with a past object by way of object condition:
one reviews the past divine eye; one reviews the divine ear-element;
one reviews the knowledge of supernormal powers with a past object that has a present object; one reviews the knowledge of penetration of minds. Noble ones [review] with a present object...
They review abandoned defilements; they review suppressed defilements; they know previously practiced defilements.
With a present object, one contemplates past aggregates as impermanent … [etc. … one contemplates them with insight, relishes them, and delights in them;
taking that as an object, lust with a past object arises … [etc. … mental distress arises. [This occurs] with a present object.
Past aggregates are related to knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of recollection of past lives, and knowledge of the destination according to karma,
as well as to adverting, by way of object-condition.
A state having a present object is related to a state having a future object by way of object-condition— namely, the future...
One reviews the divine eye; one reviews the divine ear-element;
one reviews future knowledge of the modes of supernormal power (iddhividha-ñāṇa) which has a present object;

[one reviews] knowledge of the penetration of minds …pe… one contemplates with insight the future aggregates that have present objects as their object, as impermanent …pe… taking that as an object, lust arises with a future object …pe…
Mental distress arises. Future aggregates with present objects are related to knowledge of others' minds, knowledge of future destinies, and adverting by way of object condition.
Dominance.
A state with a past object is a condition for a state with a past object by way of predominance-condition (adhipatipaccaya):
as object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati) and as conascent-predominance (sahajātādhipati). As object-predominance: one esteems and reviews past infinite consciousness (viññāṇañcāyatana);
one esteems and reviews the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (nevasaññānāsaññāyatana). [Also,] past supernormal power knowledge (iddhividhañāṇa) with a past object...
One esteems and reviews [them]; one esteems and reviews the knowledge of penetration into others' minds... the knowledge of recollection of past lives...
the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings according to their kamma. Regarding past objects, one esteems, relishes, and delights in past aggregates;
esteeming them, lust with a past object arises, and wrong view arises. Co-nascent predominance: predominance with a past object.
It is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
A state with a past object is a condition for a state with a future object by way of predominance-condition. As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*):
having taken the future base of infinite consciousness as venerable … [and so on] … the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception … [and so on] … a past object, the future …

Having treated the knowledge of the modes of psychic power as important … the knowledge of penetration into others' minds … the knowledge of recollection of past lives … the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their karma … one relishes and delights in the future aggregates that have past objects as important.
Having treated them as important, lust with a future object arises, and wrong view arises.
A state with a future object is a condition for a state with a future object by way of predominance condition: as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. As object-predominance:

having revered future supernormal knowledge (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*) with a future object … [and so on] … having revered knowledge of others' minds (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*) … [and so on] … one reviews future knowledge of the future (*anāgataṃsa-ñāṇa*). In states with a future object …
One esteems, relishes, and delights in future aggregates; esteeming them, lust with a future object arises, and wrong view arises. As co-nascent predominance:
a predominance with a future object is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for the associated aggregates.
A state with a future object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state with a past object. As object-predominance:

having esteemed the supernormal power-knowledge (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*) with a past object and a future object... the knowledge of penetration into others' minds (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*)... the knowledge of future existences (*anāgataṃsa-ñāṇa*)...
having esteemed the past aggregates with future objects, one esteems them, relishes them, and delights in them; that [esteeming]...
Having done so, lust with a past object arises; a view with a past object arises.

A state with a present object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state with a present object. Conascent predominance: a predominance with a present object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for its associated aggregates.
A state with a present object is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for a state with a past object. Object-predominance: the past...
Having made the divine eye an object of esteem, one reviews it; having made the divine ear-element an object of esteem, one reviews it;

having made the knowledge of the modes of psychic power—which has a present object but is past—an object of esteem …pe… having made the knowledge of penetration into others' minds an object of esteem …pe… having made the past aggregates, which have a present object, an object of esteem, one relishes them and delights in them; that—
Taking it as an object of esteem, lust arises with the past as its object; wrong view arises.
A state having the present as its object is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a state having the future as its object.
As object-predominance: one esteems and reviews the divine eye of the future, or the divine ear-element.

Honoring it …pe… honoring the knowledge of the modes of psychic power with a future object that has a present objective support …pe… honoring the knowledge of penetration of minds …pe… honoring the future aggregates with a present objective support, one relishes them and delights in them;
honoring them, lust with a future objective support arises, and wrong view arises.
A state with a past object is related to a state with a past object by way of proximity condition:
preceding aggregates with a past object are related to succeeding aggregates with a past object by way of proximity condition.

A state with a past object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state with a future object: a life-continuum (bhavaṅga) with a past object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for an adverting consciousness (āvajjanā) with a future object.
A state with a past object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a state with a present object:

a death-consciousness (cuticitta) with a past object is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for a rebirth-linking consciousness (paṭisandhicitta) with a present object. A state with a past object...
The life-continuum is related to advertence having a present object by way of proximity condition.
A state with a future object is related to a state with a future object by way of proximity condition:
preceding aggregates with a future object are related to succeeding aggregates with a future object by way of proximity condition.
It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
A state having a future object is a condition by way of proximity-condition for a state having a past object:

knowledge of supernormal powers having a future object [is a condition] for emergence having a past object; ... [and so on] ... knowledge of others' minds having a future object [is a condition] for [emergence] having a past object.
Knowledge of the future regarding emergence that has a past object... [and so on] ...
aggregates with a future object are related to emergence with a past object by way of proximity condition.
A state with a present object is related to a state with a present object by way of proximity condition—the preceding...
Preceding aggregates with present objects are a condition for subsequent aggregates with present objects by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Rebirth-consciousness with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) with a present object...
[and so on] ...the life-continuum with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum with a present object.
It is a condition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
A state having a present object is a condition by way of proximity-condition for a state having a past object:

a rebirth-linking consciousness with a present object is a condition for the life-continuum (*bhavanga*) with a past object; ... [and so on] ... the life-continuum with a present object is a condition for [the life-continuum] with a past object.
The life-continuum … [and so on] … present-object aggregates are a condition for emergence with past objects by way of proximity-condition (*anantarapaccaya*).
Immediate Condition:
A state with past objects is a condition for a state with past objects by way of immediate-condition (*samanantarapaccaya*). [This is the same as the proximity-condition.]

A state with a past object is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for a state with a past object; ... by way of mutuality condition; ... by way of support condition. (These three conditions are the same as in the section on "Dependent.
Strong-dependence.

A state with a past object is a condition for a state with a past object by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*)—namely, as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support …pe…. As natural decisive support:

the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having a past object, are conditions for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and [the contemplation of non-self] having a past object.
Contemplation of non-self is a condition for [the path] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state having a past object is a condition for a state having a future object by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support …pe…. As natural decisive support: contemplation of impermanence having a past object.
Contemplation of suffering and contemplation of non-self are related to future-object contemplation of impermanence, contemplation of suffering,
and contemplation of non-self by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state with a past object is related to a state with a present object by way of decisive support condition— namely, as proximity-decisive support (*anantara-upanissaya*).

Natural strong-dependence condition …pe…. Natural strong-dependence: the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having past objects, are related to the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having present objects, by way of the strong-dependence condition.
A state with a future object is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state with a future object:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, natural decisive support ... [etc. ... Natural decisive support:

the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having a future object, are conditions for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, which have a future object.
It is a condition for the contemplation of non-self by way of the decisive-support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state having a future object is a condition for a state having a past object by way of the decisive-support condition—namely, as an object-decisive-support, a proximity-decisive-support, or a natural-decisive-support (*pakatūpanissaya*) …pe….
As a natural-decisive-support: the contemplation of impermanence having a future object.
Contemplation of suffering and contemplation of non-self are related to past-object contemplation of impermanence, contemplation of suffering,
and contemplation of non-self by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
A state with a future object is related to a state with a present object by way of decisive support condition.

Natural strong-dependence (*pakatūpanissaya*): Contemplation of impermanence, suffering, and non-self with a future object is a condition, by way of strong-dependence condition, for contemplation of impermanence, suffering, and non-self with a present object.
A state with a present object is a condition, by way of strong-dependence condition, for a state with a present object—namely, proximity-strong-dependence (*anantarūpanissaya*).

Natural strong-dependence condition …pe…. Natural strong-dependence: the contemplation of impermanence with a present object, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self with a present object, are related to the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self with a present object by way of the condition of strong-dependence.
A state with a present object is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a state with a past object:
as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support …pe…. As natural decisive support:

the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and the contemplation of non-self, having a present object, [are conditions] for the contemplation of impermanence, the contemplation of suffering, and [the contemplation of non-self] having a past object.
Contemplation of non-self is a condition for [the contemplation of impermanence] by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

A state having a present object is a condition for a state having a future object by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*) and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) …pe….
Natural decisive support: contemplation of impermanence and contemplation of suffering having a present object.

Contemplation of non-self is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for future contemplation of impermanence, contemplation of suffering, and contemplation of non-self.
Repetition...
A state with a past object is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for a state with a past object:
preceding aggregates with a past object are a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for subsequent aggregates with a past object.
A state with a future object is a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for a state with a future object: preceding... [text truncated]
Preceding aggregates with future objects are a condition for subsequent aggregates with future objects by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).
A state with present objects is a condition for a state with present objects by way of the condition of repetition— preceding...
Aggregates with past objects are a condition, by way of repetition-condition, for subsequent aggregates with present objects.
Kamma...
A state with a past object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a past object: as co-nascent and as asynchronous. As co-nascent:
volition with a past object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates. At the moment of rebirth-linking … [etc.
… As asynchronous: volition with a past object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with a past object.

A state with a past object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a future object. (Asynchronous: Volition with a past object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with a future object.

A state with a past object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a present object. (Asynchronous: Volition with a past object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with a present object.
A state having a future object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state having a future object:
[this is] both conascent and asynchronous. As conascent: volition having a future object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.
As asynchronous: volition having a future object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the resultant aggregates having a future object.
Condition by way of kamma-condition:

A state having a future object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state having a past object. Asynchronous: volition having a future object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates having a past object.

A state having a future object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state having a present object. Asynchronous: volition having a future object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates having a present object.
A state with a present object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a present object—either as co-nascent or at different moments.
As co-nascent: volition with a present object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for the associated aggregates.
At the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc. ... As at different moments: volition with a present object is a condition for the resultant [aggregates].
Aggregates having present objects are related to aggregates having present objects by way of kamma-condition.

A state having a present object is related to a state having a past object by way of kamma-condition. By way of asynchronous [kamma]: volition having a present object is related to resultant aggregates having a past object by way of kamma-condition.

A state with a present object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a future object. As asynchronous: volition with a present object is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for resultant aggregates with a future object.
Resultant, etc.:

In the Pure Conditioned Relations (Suddha Hetu),
there are three in the root condition, nine in the object condition, seven in the predominance condition, seven in the proximity condition, and seven in the contiguity condition.

With regard to co-nascence, mutuality, and dependence, there are three; with regard to decisive support, nine; with regard to repetition, three; with regard to kamma, nine; with regard to result, three; with regard to nutriment, three;
with regard to faculty, jhāna, path, and association, three; with regard to presence, three; with regard to absence, seven; with regard to disappearance, seven;
with regard to non-disappearance, three. (Thus they should be counted.)
Positive Order.
Negative-Exclusion (Paccanīyuddhāra):
A state with a past object is related to a state with a past object by way of object-condition, conascence-condition, decisive-support-condition, and kamma-condition.

A state with a past object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a future object; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition, for a state with a future object; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a future object.

A state with a past object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a present object; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition, for a state with a present object; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a present object.

A state with a future object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a future object; it is a condition, by way of conascence-condition; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition.

A state with a future object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a past object; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition.
A state with a future object is related to a state with a present object by way of object condition, decisive support condition, and kamma condition.
A state with a present object is related to a state with a present object by way of object condition, conascence condition, decisive support condition, and kamma condition.

A state with a present object is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a state with a past object; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*), for a state with a past object; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition (*kammapaccaya*), for a state with a past object.

A state with a present object is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state with a future object; it is a condition, by way of decisive support-condition, for a state with a future object; it is a condition, by way of kamma-condition, for a state with a future object. 1.20.7.2.
